conventions.offset: Addresses are PRINTED addresses. The Modbus frame address is address_start + wire_offset for the register's space (-1 for data and settings, 0 for model). Both apps currently store the already-offset value, which is why their labels read one low.
conventions.identity: PV data and settings SHARE address numbers — 3000 is 'Product model' on 0x04 and 'Year' on 0x03. A register is identified by (space, address), never by address alone.
conventions.width: Width comes from the data-type column, not the printed address span. A span with a 16-bit type is a RANGE of 16-bit registers, not one wide register.
conventions.precedence: overrides > app value > document (newest first). When the two apps disagree with each other, the document breaks the tie.
conventions.valid_range: `valid_range` is a WRITE limit, and only settings carry one. Its single source is the extension's PV_SETTINGS_CONTROL_MAP — the documents print no limits at all, and Tauri has none. A setting with a `value_map` and no `valid_range` is bounded by its codes, not missing a limit. Never read the `1->100` in a description as a range: that is `scale`.

register_spaces.note: PV operational information. Printed addresses; subtract 1 for the frame.

registers.description: For 80-110K MAX/PRO internal voltage calibration applications; Voltage calibration strategy: 1. registers.revision_note: In RS485_MODBUS Solis PV Grid-Connected Inverter.pdf this was u16; updated to u16. In [Grid-Tied EN 2022.1.20]RS485_MODBUS(INV-3000ID EPM-36000ID) PV Grid Tied Inverter.pdf this was ascii; updated to u16. Serial number as TEXT, not a number. The 2020, 2021 and 2022 documents all type it ASCII, and every other document spells the decode out: '3230 = 01, 3231 = 23, Display: 0123' — one character per byte, two per register, across 3230-3249. Extension had u32 and Tauri u16; both render digits as meaningless integers. NOTE this is a DIFFERENT register from the SN at 3061-3064, which the documents call 'Inverter sequence (hexadecimal display)' and which is genuinely hex, not ASCII. Confirmed by Tanner 2026-08-20.

registers.revision_note: Was keyed `add35000` in both apps. There is no add-35000 setting register: six documents print 3028 as 'Restart the HMI', and 35000 is a read-only model register in section 5.1 read with 0x04 and NO offset (see the `model` space). The apps' 2999 base put index 28 on the wire at 3027, which the documents call 'DRM ON/OFF', so the extension's PvDeviceWidget 'Model Type' row was decoding a DRM value through INVERTER_MODEL_TYPE_MAP. Renamed here; both apps must drop `add35000` and read 35000 from the model space instead.

registers.revision_note:
scale 1 -> 0.01, unit '%', 2026-08-22. PROVEN, unlike its neighbours: V18 and V19 print '0.01%' in this register's unit column. (V17 and the older Grid-Tied files print '1%'; the bare '0.001'/'0.01' readings in the extraction cache are a mis-parsed adjacent column.) The valid_range agrees -- -6000..+6000 raw for a documented -60%..+60%.

Six sibling registers were changed to 0.01 in the same pass on the strength of the description wording alone and have since been REVERTED. SCALE LESSON FOR THIS REGISTER FAMILY, recorded 2026-08-22 after a wrong call was caught by field evidence:

The description wording '10000 <--> 100%' does NOT reliably imply a scale of 0.01 on the working-mode percentage registers. Twelve PV registers with that exact wording do derive 0.01, which made it look like a convention -- it is not one. The signal that DOES establish the scale is the unit COLUMN in V18/V19: where those print '0.01%' the scale is 0.01, and where they print '1%' or a bare '1' it is 1.

THE FIELD EVIDENCE: a SolisCloud Volt-var page read off a real inverter showed 3142 Q1 (Max Leading) = 30% and 3143 Q4 (Max Lagging) = -30%. SolisCloud renders the RAW register word and applies no scaling of its own -- corroborated on the same screen by 3138-3141 V1-V4 reading 119.5 / 127 / 144.3 / 153 V, sensible grid voltages at the map's scale 0.1. A +/-30% clamp is an ordinary Volt-var setting, so the raw words really are 30 and -30, which means scale 1. Under 0.01 the raw words would have had to be 3000 and -3000 and SolisCloud would have shown that.

So the Volt-var axis is genuinely ASYMMETRIC and this is not an artefact: the outer clamps 3142/3143 are scale 1, while the inner setpoints 3128/3129 are 0.01 (and those two DO print '0.01%' in V18/V19). Do not 'tidy' that asymmetry away.

DOMAIN RULE for sanity-checking this family: a POWER FACTOR register is signed and runs -0.8 through 1 to +0.8; a REACTIVE POWER register is signed and is a percentage of rated. By that rule 3146 PFcSet is a power factor and its 0.01 scale is correct for the 0.8-1.0 range.

name and value_map CORRECTED 2026-08-22.

NAME: read 'Working Status', which is the DATA-space 0x04 register at the same printed address -- a read-only status enum nobody can write. It bled across the space collision during the harvest. The document row is unambiguous: '3072 Day Time PID Switch U16 0xAA ON' (V17 p20, Grid-Tied 2022.1.20 p30), and the row continues '...with Day Time PID Solution', which corroborates the existing key.

VALUE_MAP: Tauri carried {0 Disabled, 1 Enabled}. It is a MAGIC VALUE register like 3070 and 3071 beside it -- 0xAA (170) ON, 0x55 (85) OFF. Writing 1 does nothing at all, so the boolean rendering was not merely mislabelled, it was inoperative.

The key `dayTimePidSwitch` is UNCHANGED -- it is the localStorage key.

registers.revision_note:
SCALE LESSON FOR THIS REGISTER FAMILY, recorded 2026-08-22 after a wrong call was caught by field evidence:

The description wording '10000 <--> 100%' does NOT reliably imply a scale of 0.01 on the working-mode percentage registers. Twelve PV registers with that exact wording do derive 0.01, which made it look like a convention -- it is not one. The signal that DOES establish the scale is the unit COLUMN in V18/V19: where those print '0.01%' the scale is 0.01, and where they print '1%' or a bare '1' it is 1.

THE FIELD EVIDENCE: a SolisCloud Volt-var page read off a real inverter showed 3142 Q1 (Max Leading) = 30% and 3143 Q4 (Max Lagging) = -30%. SolisCloud renders the RAW register word and applies no scaling of its own -- corroborated on the same screen by 3138-3141 V1-V4 reading 119.5 / 127 / 144.3 / 153 V, sensible grid voltages at the map's scale 0.1. A +/-30% clamp is an ordinary Volt-var setting, so the raw words really are 30 and -30, which means scale 1. Under 0.01 the raw words would have had to be 3000 and -3000 and SolisCloud would have shown that.

So the Volt-var axis is genuinely ASYMMETRIC and this is not an artefact: the outer clamps 3142/3143 are scale 1, while the inner setpoints 3128/3129 are 0.01 (and those two DO print '0.01%' in V18/V19). Do not 'tidy' that asymmetry away.

DOMAIN RULE for sanity-checking this family: a POWER FACTOR register is signed and runs -0.8 through 1 to +0.8; a REACTIVE POWER register is signed and is a percentage of rated. By that rule 3146 PFcSet is a power factor and its 0.01 scale is correct for the 0.8-1.0 range.

registers.revision_note:
SCALE LESSON FOR THIS REGISTER FAMILY, recorded 2026-08-22 after a wrong call was caught by field evidence:

The description wording '10000 <--> 100%' does NOT reliably imply a scale of 0.01 on the working-mode percentage registers. Twelve PV registers with that exact wording do derive 0.01, which made it look like a convention -- it is not one. The signal that DOES establish the scale is the unit COLUMN in V18/V19: where those print '0.01%' the scale is 0.01, and where they print '1%' or a bare '1' it is 1.

THE FIELD EVIDENCE: a SolisCloud Volt-var page read off a real inverter showed 3142 Q1 (Max Leading) = 30% and 3143 Q4 (Max Lagging) = -30%. SolisCloud renders the RAW register word and applies no scaling of its own -- corroborated on the same screen by 3138-3141 V1-V4 reading 119.5 / 127 / 144.3 / 153 V, sensible grid voltages at the map's scale 0.1. A +/-30% clamp is an ordinary Volt-var setting, so the raw words really are 30 and -30, which means scale 1. Under 0.01 the raw words would have had to be 3000 and -3000 and SolisCloud would have shown that.

So the Volt-var axis is genuinely ASYMMETRIC and this is not an artefact: the outer clamps 3142/3143 are scale 1, while the inner setpoints 3128/3129 are 0.01 (and those two DO print '0.01%' in V18/V19). Do not 'tidy' that asymmetry away.

DOMAIN RULE for sanity-checking this family: a POWER FACTOR register is signed and runs -0.8 through 1 to +0.8; a REACTIVE POWER register is signed and is a percentage of rated. By that rule 3146 PFcSet is a power factor and its 0.01 scale is correct for the 0.8-1.0 range.

value_map.0: Non-stop OFF (inverter stops on PV insulation fault)

registers.revision_note:
RECOVERED 2026-08-22. This register was missing from the map entirely, suppressed by a stale 'Reserve' range -- see the note on the pv_merge fix. It is printed in V19 page 43 (wire 3174).

Three values, and the third is a different KIND of thing from the other two: 0x00 and 0x01 are a persistent setting that survives a power cycle, while 0x2A is a momentary ACTION that clears latched fault information and explicitly does NOT have the power-off saving function. Default 0.

This is the register behind SolisCloud's Device Maintenance page, which shows two 'Set' actions both at Modbus 3175. Note the map substantiates ONE clear action (0x2A), not two: no document gives a separate code for a 'PVGndRun' clear, so whatever the second row writes is unproven and must not be guessed at.

registers.name: MPPT 6 current
registers.revision_note:
key corrected 7 -> 6, 2026-08-22. The settings-space keys for the MPPT current block ran ONE TOO HIGH: this address was keyed 'mppt7Current' while its own name, and the data register at the same printed address, both say MPPT 6.

The addresses are the tiebreak. The DATA space runs MPPT 1..16 over printed 3530..3546, one per address, so 3535 is MPPT 6 and 3544 is MPPT 15. The settings NAMES agree with that at every shared address; only the keys were out, so the NAME was right and the KEY was wrong. The off-by-one comes from Tauri's settingMapper, which keys index 535 as 'mppt7Current'.

This matters because the key IS the localStorage key: left alone, MPPT 6's current would be filed and read back under MPPT 7.

This matters because the key IS the localStorage key: left alone, MPPT 15's current would be filed and read back under MPPT 16.
